newsitem.title: USA: Whittaker mulls unit spin-off, debt cuts.
newsitem.headline: Whittaker mulls unit spin-off, debt cuts.

text.p: Whittaker Corp Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Joseph Alibrandi said the company had hired an investment adviser to assist it in exploring strategic options, including a potential spin-off, sale or merger of its Xyplex Networks subsidiary.
He also told the New York Society of Security Analysts that the company was cutting costs in all business units and monetizing assets, including certain real estate holdings, to cut down its debt.
The company hoped to pay down debt by as much as $40 million to $50 million this fiscal year, he said. It said its debt now stood at $146 million.

Alibrandi also said the company would be divesting all or part of its defense electronics unit over the coming months, because a continued downturn in the U.S. defense budget which had hurt Whittaker's defense electronics equipment sales.
The defense electronics unit made specialized command and control, communications and survivability systems.

But the company's core aerospace business was still performing well, Alibrandi said. He said the projected growth of commercial aircraft production over the next five to 10 years would bode well for the company, which made fluid control valves and heat sensors.
Its Xyplex unit makes remote access and internet working products and technology for the telecommunications industry.
Xyplex recently announced its new EdgeBlaster remote access server targeted for use later this year by internet service providers and office users worldwide.
